vignette: Emmanuel, a 77-year-old African man and software engineer, has lived through experiences that have deeply imprinted his life. Born in the midst of political turmoil in his home country, he witnessed violence and upheaval from an early age. At 30, Emmanuel fled the conflict with his wife, Amina, leaving behind their small village and most of their possessions to seek refuge in a neighboring country. This journey was marked by constant fear and uncertainty, as they navigated through treacherous landscapes and encountered hostile forces. Today, Emmanuel's life is punctuated by intrusive memories of that harrowing time. He often finds himself reliving the moments when he heard gunshots echoing in the distance or saw fellow refugees being brutalized. While working at his desk, seemingly mundane sounds like a loud noise from the building can instantly transport him back to those terrifying days. The sensation is so vivid that it leaves him shaking and breathless, clutching his chest as if reliving the physical strain of fleeing danger. Emmanuel’s nights are restless; his sleep is frequently interrupted by nightmares where he and Amina are running through dark forests or hiding from soldiers. These dreams leave him drenched in sweat and struggling to catch his breath, often waking up before dawn and unable to fall back asleep due to persistent anxiety. The next day at work, Emmanuel feels drained and less effective as a software engineer, finding it difficult to concentrate on complex coding tasks. Despite the challenges, Emmanuel has always been proud of his work in technology. His role involves debugging code and troubleshooting systems, a meticulous process that requires intense focus and patience. However, since returning from his traumatic experiences, he finds himself hyper-vigilant at work, constantly on edge, scanning his environment for potential threats. This heightened state of alertness makes it hard to maintain the level of concentration needed for his job. Emmanuel’s relationship with Amina has also been affected by his PTSD symptoms. He often avoids discussing their past or reminiscing about events from those turbulent years. While this might seem like a coping mechanism, it strains their intimacy and communication. Amina feels that they are growing apart as Emmanuel increasingly withdraws into himself, spending long hours working late to avoid conversations he finds too triggering. Recently, Emmanuel has experienced intense survivor’s guilt, questioning why he was able to escape while so many others were not. This guilt gnaws at him, making it difficult for him to enjoy his current life and the comforts they now have in their new home. He often wonders if he deserves the peace and stability he now enjoys, given what happened back then. Emmanuel’s days are filled with a sense of unreality, as if he is detached from his surroundings. His memories of the trauma feel more vivid than his current reality, leading him to isolate himself further. He avoids social gatherings or events that remind him of the chaos and violence he experienced, preferring instead to stay home where he can control his environment. Despite these challenges, Emmanuel remains resilient. He continues to work diligently as a software engineer, finding solace in the logic and order of technology. While his PTSD symptoms persistently impact his life, Emmanuel holds onto hope that with time, he will find ways to integrate his past into a more peaceful present. In moments of quiet reflection, Emmanuel often thinks about how far he has come since those desperate days as a refugee. He is grateful for Amina’s unwavering support and the relative safety they now enjoy. Though the trauma still haunts him, Emmanuel clings to hope that there can be healing, even if it comes slowly and in small doses.
